title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: Charred marinated chicken in a spiced tomato and cream sauce
excerpt: The most popular Indian restaurant dish in the UK: chicken thighs marinated in yogurt and spices, grilled until charred, then added to a rich, mildly spiced tomato and cream sauce. The tikka (charred chicken) element is what separates this from a simple curry.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is a dish of disputed origin, often claimed to have been invented in Britain (possibly in Glasgow) when a customer complained that the chicken tikka was too dry and a cook improvised a sauce from tinned tomato soup and spices. Others contend that the dish has roots in Indian cooking traditions, citing similar preparations in Punjabi and Mughal cuisine. Whatever its origin, CTM became the most ordered Indian restaurant dish in the UK, a cultural phenomenon described at its peak as Britain's true national dish. The critical element is the tikka: the chicken must be marinated and then grilled or broiled at high heat until genuinely charred in spots. This char provides a smoky depth that cannot be replicated by simply simmering raw chicken in the sauce. The masala sauce is mild enough for wide appeal; kashmiri chilli powder (which gives colour more than heat) and cream provide the characteristic red-orange colour and gentle richness.

recipeTools.notes: A large frying pan or wide saucepan for the masala sauce.

content.text: The char on the chicken is not decoration; it is a structural part of the flavour. Grill the chicken under the highest possible heat or on a griddle pan until blackened in places. Do not skip or moderate this step. The sauce should cook until the oil visibly separates from the masala before the cream goes in; this tells you the tomatoes are properly cooked.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless; cut into 4 cm chunks
1 tsp for marinade, 1 tsp for sauce

content.text: Marinate the chicken: mix the yogurt, 1 teaspoon of garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice, and 0.5 teaspoon of salt. Add the chicken and coat well. Marinate for at least 1 hour or overnight. Grill or griddle the chicken under the highest heat, in a single layer, for 5 to 6 minutes per side until charred in patches and cooked through. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 18 minutes until very deeply golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon of garam masala and cook for 1 minute. Add the blended tomatoes and 1 teaspoon of salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until very thick and the oil separates.

Add the cream and 100 ml water and stir to combine. Add the grilled chicken and any resting juices. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve over basmati rice or with naan, scattered with fresh coriander.
